images.title: One more row adds a whole row
images.purpose: Shows that laying one more row along a tray of 23 rows of 27 mangoes adds 27 mangoes, because a product is a rectangle of rows and columns.
images.composition: One large rectangle block centred, with one thin strip just below it, separated by a small gap. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A large teal (#0072B2) filled rectangle block, 27 units wide and 23 units tall, with a thin dark outline. The label '27' sits centred above the top edge with a thin grey double arrow spanning the width; the label '23' sits to the left of the block with a thin grey double arrow spanning the height. Just below the block, after a small gap, one amber (#E69F00) strip exactly as wide as the block (27 units) and 1 unit tall. To the right of the amber strip the label '+ 27', and under it the label 'one more row'. Exactly 1 block and 1 strip.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A product is a rectangle, so one more row adds a whole row of 27.
images.description: Shows that laying one more row along a tray of 23 rows of 27 mangoes adds 27 mangoes, because a product is a rectangle of rows and columns.

image_decisions.why: The hook idea is spatial: seeing the product as a rectangle makes it obvious that one more row adds 27.
